Life cycle of a grasshopper. A circular diagram with three main stages. 1. An adult grasshopper depositing a pod of eggs into the soil. 2. A tiny nymph hatching from the egg, looking like a wingless grasshopper. 3. An adult grasshopper with fully developed wings feeding on a green leaf. Arrows connect Egg to Nymph to Adult, and back to Egg.

Life cycle of a maize weevil. A circular diagram with four stages centered around a maize grain. 1. Egg: A cross-section of a maize grain showing a tiny egg laid inside a sealed hole. 2. Larva: A fat, white, legless grub eating the inside of the grain. 3. Pupa: A resting pupa inside the hollowed grain. 4. Adult: A dark-brown weevil with a distinct snout emerging from a round exit hole in the grain.

A four-panel illustration showing pesticide modes of action. 1. Stomach Poison: A caterpillar chewing on a leaf that has chemical droplets on the surface, with a skull/crossbones inside its stomach. 2. Contact Poison: A beetle walking over a sprayed surface, with chemical droplets absorbing through its legs and back. 3. Systemic Poison: An aphid sucking sap from a stem; arrows show the chemical moving from the roots, up the stem, and into the aphid. 4. Fumigant: Gas clouds surrounding a weevil inside a closed silo container.
